Hi team, adding privacy guidance below.

# *Direct marketing*

The initial communication inviting drivers to participate in the competition qualifies as direct marketing, as it promotes a Bolt-run initiative to identifiable drivers. For Lithuania, Bolt may rely on soft opt-in, provided that:

* The message contains a clear *unsubscribe option*; and
* The content is strictly related to Bolt’s own mobility services.

Please ensure the invitation includes unsubscribe instructions in line with our standard direct marketing requirements.

*_Important_*: The invitation message constitutes direct marketing. Drivers who have opted out of marketing must not receive this communication. Please ensure marketing suppression lists are applied before sending the campaign. 

# *Participation form*

The form used to join the competition is not a marketing consent mechanism. It should only collect the minimum data necessary to register the driver (e.g., driver ID or contact details) and must not introduce any additional consent requests.

# *Data used to run the competition*

Trip counts, safety-related signals, fraud indicators, and complaint history are all data that Bolt already processes for service provision, safety, and platform integrity. It is covered under our [Privacy Notice for Drivers|https://bolt.eu/lt-lt/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/].

Using this information to determine rankings and eligibility is compatible with those existing purposes and does not require new consent.

The T&Cs should transparently summarise which categories of data are used to evaluate performance and to determine disqualification grounds.

# *Transparency*

As I mentioned, our Privacy Notice for Drivers already covers such use-cases, and therefore my suggestion is to supplement the T&Cs with a link to the privacy notice:

{quote}The processing of personal data in connection with your participation in the competition is carried out in accordance with the Bolt [Privacy Notice for Drivers|https://bolt.eu/lt-lt/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/].{quote}

T&Cs should be easily accessible to drivers. You may link them directly in the invitation or attach them to the participation form.

I’ve requested access to the document shared by [~accountid:5d95f00136d2520dde7ede17] , and when we’ll have the final version of T&C, I will add the necessary privacy clause(s).

# *Retention*

Any temporary ranking or competition-specific files should be deleted once the prize is awarded unless needed to resolve disputes or meet audit obligations.

❗ Important - if any of this data will be kept in a Google sheet, *please make sure to have access to the sheet limited to people who need the access, and not “everyone with the link”.* 

*Conclusion*
From a privacy perspective, the competition can proceed as long as:

* The marketing invitation includes an unsubscribe option,
* Comms honour drivers' marketing preferences,
* The participation form collects only minimal data,
* We include privacy clauses to the T&Cs.

Happy to review the T&Cs / the communication drafts before they go out.

They say that there is *no market practice* for refunding inspection rides and confirmed that any voluntary refund mechanism would be a *commercial choice*, not a legal duty (as it is the obligation of the transport provider to ensure the control rights and bear the costs of the free ride). If Bolt chooses to refund, counsel recommends requiring *proper inspector identification and an inspection protocol/record* as evidence. 

Please see [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1oT7fStubr-LJxKq0N6TO1lVal9GyJf0-DafoSjlbr8o/edit?tab=t.0] their full comments.

I've reviewed the case and everything is correct on Bolt's end. The preauthorisation was successfully released, and there is no further action required from us.

Please follow the steps in this Knowledge Base article to advise the customer: [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/7109163016850?country=global&language=en|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/7109163016850?country=global&language=en]

Advise the customer to *check with their bank* to confirm the release of the preauthorisation. Banks handle these releases differently, and while some are immediate, others may process it as a temporary charge that is then refunded. Sometimes, the payment is reversed without the bank sending a reversal notification to the customer, which might lead the user to think that the reversal has not been made.

The reversal can take up to *30 days* to complete, as pending authorisations typically expire after that time on banks end.

Unfortunately, we don't have full visibility into all the parties involved in the payment processing beyond our payment partner. Therefore, we can't track the exact status of the preauthorisation release once it has been sent.

Thank you,

Afiba

Advise the customer to *check with their bank* to confirm the release of the preauthorisation. Sometimes, the payment is reversed without the bank sending a reversal notification to the customer, which might lead the user to think that the reversal has not been made.

The reversal can take up to *30 days* to complete, as pending authorisations typically expire after that time on banks end.

Hello Team!

I completely understand why this might look like a double charge, but I can assure you that the user was only charged once. This is a common part of how card payments are processed. Here's what happens:

# When the user first makes a payment, the bank temporarily ‘reserves' the funds and this is just the bank setting aside the amount for the transaction. The user’s account balance might show less amount but the payment hasn’t actually been taken out by the bank yet.
# Later, when the payment is fully processed, that reserved amount is now “officially” debited from the user’s account. At that point, some banks send a second notification, which can make it seem like a second charge.


The refund is successfully completed. I would advise the user to check their final account balance or statement, where they can confirm that only one payment was actually withdrawn. The earlier “pending” amount will either drop off or convert into the final charge.

Cheers,
Afiba
